schemaVersion: Ehel Stage 1 Art & Design Placement Exam v1.0
subject: Art & Design
title: Stage 1 Art & Design Starting Check
description: A short, friendly check of how you see colours, shapes, lines and textures, and how you use art tools, so we know where to start and where a grown-up can help.
attemptsAllowed: Unlimited - this check finds your starting point; it is never a fail
feedbackMode: Immediate child-friendly feedback with a starting-point report
_comment: Two fields beyond the shared placement shape, both optional and both for a reader of five: `pic` on a question is a picture drawn above it (emoji), and `optionPics` is one picture per option in the same order as `options` - an emoji, `mark:<kind>` for a line drawn by the lesson kit's own mark previews, or `swatch:<hex>` for a patch of colour. The text of every option is still there, so the key is the same text the other subjects' keys are. Built into starting-check.html by ../lesson-kit/build-check.py and checked by ../lesson-kit/check-coverage.py.

ready.label: Ready for Stage 1
ready.message: Brilliant looking! You know your colours, shapes and lines like a real artist. Start with Lesson 1 and have fun.

readyWithReview.label: Ready, with a grown-up close by
readyWithReview.message: You are ready to start. Do the lessons below with a grown-up close by, and take your time.

notReady.label: Let's look and make together first
notReady.message: Let's start slowly. Do Lesson 1 with a grown-up beside you, and look for colours, shapes and lines together every day.

recommendation.label: Stage 1 Art & Design, Lesson 1 with a grown-up

sections.title: Colours and shapes
sections.description: Can you name the colours you see, find a shape, and see what comes next in a pattern?

sections.title: Lines, marks and touch
sections.description: Can you tell one kind of line from another, pick the right tool for a mark, and say how something feels?

sections.title: Making and looking
sections.description: Do you know the tools for cutting and sticking, can you say what is in a picture, and say something kind about it?

questions.question: Which one is red?
questions.explanation: Red is the colour of a strawberry and a fire engine.

questions.question: Which one is a circle?
questions.options: a triangle | a circle | a square
questions.explanation: A circle is round all the way, with no corners.

questions.question: What colour is grass?
questions.explanation: Grass is green, like a leaf.

questions.question: Red, blue, red, blue. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Red, blue, red, blue, red. The pattern says it again.

questions.question: Which one is a wavy line?
questions.options: a straight line | a wavy line | a zigzag
questions.explanation: A wavy line goes up and down gently, like the sea.

questions.question: Which one is a zigzag?
questions.explanation: A zigzag turns sharply, up and down, like lightning.

questions.question: Which one feels rough and bumpy?
questions.options: a feather | a rock | a teddy
questions.explanation: A rock is rough and bumpy. A feather and a teddy are soft.

questions.question: Which one would you use to draw a thin line?
questions.options: a sponge | a pencil | your whole hand
questions.explanation: A pencil has a thin point, so it makes a thin line.

questions.question: What do you use to cut paper?
questions.explanation: Scissors cut paper. Hold them carefully, with a grown-up close by.

questions.question: What do you use to stick two pieces of paper together?
questions.explanation: Glue sticks things together. Water would just make the paper wet.

questions.question: Look at the picture. What can you see in it?
questions.options: a car and a boat | a house, a tree and the sun | a cat and a dog
questions.correctAnswer: a house, a tree and the sun
questions.explanation: A house, a tree and the sun. Looking closely is what artists do.

questions.question: Your friend shows you a picture of a bright red sun. Which is a kind thing to say?
questions.options: I did not look. | I like the bright red sun. | That is bad.
questions.correctAnswer: I like the bright red sun.
questions.explanation: Saying what you like, and what is really there, is kind and true.
